action: In general, a standard system update will make all the necessary changes.
description:
USN-9064-1 fixed vulnerabilities in Pillow. Unfortunately, the fix for
CVE-2026-112402 introduced a regression that caused resizing images with
the NEAREST filter, and resizing any "1" or "P" mode image, to fail. This
update fixes the problem.

We apologize for the inconvenience.

Original advisory details:

 It was discovered that Pillow could enter an infinite loop while
 determining the frame count of a MIC image. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. This issue
 only affected Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, and
 Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-112390)

 It was discovered that Pillow's PdfParser.get_value() could recurse
 without a limit while reading nested PDF objects. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. This issue
 only affected Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS,
 Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 18.04 LTS.
 (CVE-2026-112391)

 It was discovered that Pillow's rank-based filters could dereference
 invalid image storage for a zero-size image. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to cause a crash. (CVE-2026-112392)

 It was discovered that Pillow had a heap buffer overflow in
 _tiffWriteProc when saving compressed TIFF data. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to crash the process or execute arbitrary
 code. (CVE-2026-112393)

 It was discovered that Pillow's P;2L and P;4L raw decoders could
 read past the end of an input buffer. An attacker could possibly
 use this issue to disclose heap memory or crash the process.
 (CVE-2026-112394)

 It was discovered that Pillow's tiled-TIFF decoder could read past
 the tile buffer while copying four-byte pixels. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to expose heap data or crash the process.
 This issue only affected Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Ubuntu
 24.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-112395)

 It was discovered that Pillow had a heap use-after-free when libtiff
 rejects a tag while encoding TIFF data to an in-memory buffer. An
 attacker could possibly use this issue to crash the process or
 execute arbitrary code. This issue only affected Ubuntu 26.10 and
 Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-112396)

 It was discovered that Pillow's ImageMorph.MorphOp.apply() could
 access memory before a row buffer for a zero-width image. An
 attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a crash.
 (CVE-2026-112397)

 It was discovered that Pillow's FlashPix JPEG-tile decoder could
 write decoded scanlines beyond the allocated tile buffer. An
 attacker could possibly use this issue to corrupt heap memory and
 execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2026-112398)

 It was discovered that Pillow could allocate an APNG disposal
 background at the full canvas size before applying the
 decompression-bomb check. An attacker could possibly use this
 issue to exhaust memory and cause a denial of service. This issue
 only affected Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS,
 and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-112399)

 It was discovered that Pillow could retain a rejected GIF frame
 size after a decompression-bomb exception. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to exhaust memory and cause a denial of
 service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS,
 and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-112400)

 It was discovered that Pillow performed quadratic copying while
 parsing GIF comments. An attacker could possibly use this issue
 to cause a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu
 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, and
 Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-112401)

 It was discovered that Pillow could double free image memory when
 ImagingScaleAffine encounters a selective allocation failure. An
 attacker could possibly use this issue to crash the process.
 (CVE-2026-112402)

 It was discovered that Pillow's JPEG decoder could write a
 full-width scanline into a buffer sized for a requested draft
 scale. An attacker could possibly use this issue to corrupt heap
 memory or execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2026-112403)

 It was discovered that Pillow's TIFF tile and RGBA decode paths
 could read beyond row data produced by libtiff. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to expose heap data or crash the process.
 This issue only affected Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Ubuntu
 24.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-112404)

 It was discovered that Pillow's Image.merge() could dereference a
 null image8 plane. An attacker could possibly use this issue to
 cause a crash. This issue only affected Ubuntu 26.10 and Ubuntu
 26.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-112405)

 It was discovered that Pillow could enter an infinite loop while
 rewriting PDF pages. An attacker could possibly use this issue to
 cause a denial of service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 26.10,
 Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 20.04
 LTS, and Ubuntu 18.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-112406)

 It was discovered that Pillow performed quadratic copying when
 saving a GIF with a long comment. An attacker could possibly use
 this issue to cause a denial of service. This issue only affected
 Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS.
 (CVE-2026-112891)

 It was discovered that Pillow's MSP RLE decoder could expand a
 small file into an unbounded in-memory buffer. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to exhaust memory and cause a denial of
 service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS,
 Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, and Ubuntu
 18.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-112892)

 It was discovered that Pillow could free an invalid glyph pointer
 during FreeType rendering with an active stroker. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to corrupt memory or crash the process.
 This issue only affected Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, and
 Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-112893)

 It was discovered that Pillow took quadratic time to reserve PDF
 object identifiers when saving many frames. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. This issue
 only affected Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS,
 Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 18.04 LTS.
 (CVE-2026-112894)

 It was discovered that Pillow could exhaust resources while parsing
 an existing PDF during an append operation. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. This issue
 only affected Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS,
 Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 18.04 LTS.
 (CVE-2026-112895)

 It was discovered that Pillow's TIFF encoder could read beyond a
 ColorMap buffer when retained TIFF metadata has a plane size
 inconsistent with BitsPerSample. An attacker could possibly use
 this issue to disclose heap memory or crash the process.
 (CVE-2026-112896)

 It was discovered that Pillow could return uninitialized memory as
 pixels when libtiff performs a short decode of JPEG-compressed or
 Group 4 fax TIFF data. An attacker could possibly use this issue
 to disclose stale heap contents. This issue only affected Ubuntu
 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS.
 (CVE-2026-112897)

 It was discovered that Pillow could disclose uninitialized stack
 memory when Image.quantize() uses an empty palette. An attacker
 could possibly use this issue to obtain stack contents. This issue
 only affected Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 24.04
 LTS. (CVE-2026-112898)

 It was discovered that Pillow was vulnerable to argument injection
 when invoking Ghostscript for EPS input. An attacker could possibly
 use this issue to inject Ghostscript arguments and execute
 arbitrary commands. (CVE-2026-112900)

 It was discovered that Pillow's XBM header parser was vulnerable
 to regular-expression denial of service. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service.
 (CVE-2026-112901)

 It was discovered that Pillow could export non-contiguous image
 data to Arrow arrays. An attacker could possibly use this issue to
 disclose uninitialized memory or stale heap contents. This issue
 only affected Ubuntu 26.10 and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-114501)

 It was discovered that Pillow could overflow an integer when
 tracking glyph positions for very long strings. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to cause logic errors or resource
 consumption. This issue only affected Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Ubuntu
 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 18.04 LTS, Ubuntu 16.04 LTS,
 and Ubuntu 14.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-42308)

 It was discovered that Pillow could hang indefinitely when
 processing a malicious PDF with a trailer loop. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. This issue
 only affected Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 20.04
 LTS, and Ubuntu 18.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-42310)

 It was discovered that Pillow did not properly apply decompression
 bomb checks after seeking to new frames in MPO, DCX, and MIC
 images. An attacker could possibly use this issue to bypass the
 check and cause memory exhaustion. This issue only affected
 Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04
 LTS, Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 18.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 16.04 LTS.
 (CVE-2026-96636)

 It was discovered that Pillow did not properly apply decompression
 bomb checks after seeking to new frames in SPIDER images. An
 attacker could possibly use this issue to cause memory exhaustion.
 This issue only affected Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Ubuntu
 24.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 18.04 LTS,
 and Ubuntu 16.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-96637)

 It was discovered that Pillow's BMP RLE decoder could expand a
 small file into an unbounded in-memory buffer. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to exhaust memory and cause a denial of
 service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS,
 and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-96638)

 It was discovered that Pillow's multi-frame loaders could retain
 a stale ImagingCore allocation. An attacker could possibly use
 this issue to cause out-of-bounds writes and crashes. This issue
 only affected Ubuntu 26.10 and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-96639)

 It was discovered that Pillow did not properly detect cyclic page
 tree references in PDF parsing. An attacker could possibly use
 this issue to cause a denial of service. This issue only affected
 Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS,
 Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 18.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-96640)

 It was discovered that Pillow's PILfont text-width accumulation
 could overflow due to unchecked negative glyph advances. An
 attacker could possibly use this issue to cause logic errors or
 resource consumption. (CVE-2026-96641)

 It was discovered that Pillow's TarIO initializer accepted a
 negative octal member size. An attacker could possibly use this
 issue to cause an infinite loop and denial of service.
 (CVE-2026-96642)

 It was discovered that Pillow's Exif.load() could perform
 quadratic CPU work when processing repeated EXIF headers. An
 attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of
 service. This issue only affected Ubuntu 26.10 and Ubuntu 26.04
 LTS. (CVE-2026-96643)

 It was discovered that Pillow could call jpeg_write_marker() for a
 JPEG COM comment when an ICC profile has exactly filled the
 65536-byte encoder buffer. An attacker could possibly use this
 issue to cause a heap buffer overflow and execute arbitrary code.
 This issue only affected Ubuntu 26.10, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, and
 Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-96778)
isummary: USN-9064-1 introduced a regression in Pillow
title: Pillow regression
